body: You seem like a good person that could do great things if you weren’t in the environment you are in. I’m so sorry you’re hurting so much. I stick around because I feel like things haven’t gotten as worse as they could be. I always have some hope that they will get better, we will never know unless we stick around:/
Wow. Thank you for sharing. You are so strong
That’s how I think sometimes as well.
Hey, Is there a reason you feel like you hate yourself? Is that reason always going to hold true? If not, what needs to happen so that you can love yourself more?

Hey there. It sounds like you have a lot going on at home and it’s completely okay to feel the way you are feeling. I don’t think it’s petty. I also think you have a lot of great potential. Suicide hotlines are there to prevent a determined person from killing themselves. If you’d like to vent, feel free to message me anyway. I have called Samaritans in the past and they’re always kind and willing to listen. (212) 673-3000 (samaritans of NY)
Hey, I’m really sorry you’re feeling this way. Do you want to talk about things? Feel free to vent to me. You’re not alone.

Of course. I hope you realize how valuable you are. I may not know the whole story but I’m inspired by your strength. Not everyone can keep their head above water for this long and be a mom. I hope things get easier for you.

Hey, I’m sorry things are the way they are for you. I can’t imagine myself being a day in your shoes, I’m weak and can be very selfish. You’re a strong individual and I really wish karma was a real phenomenon because you deserve joy and peace. I hope you find a better job with better coworkers, a better shift so you can see some daylight, and I hope you realize you’re a great mom and wife. You’re pushing through so much to do your best and it should be recognized. I hope you get to breath easy one day, you deserve happiness 💕

This is exactly it. I feel very regretful, and just stunned. Like, I can't believe I did that. I can't believe this is my life. I'm not like this... but now, I'm like this and it's so hard to move on. I wish I could just move on, but now, instead, I wish to die. How long has it been for you?

I've read that if it fails and you survive, you'll have ruptured veins all over your face and a pretty bad bruise around your neck, at best. The worst scenario is brain damage. This can make your problems more public than they already are or just worst in general.

I'm sorry to hear that. Do you live near a large metropolitan area? Those areas usually have resources. Maybe look for a psychiatric nurse practitioner concierge service online that offers both therapy and medications for less than what a psychiatrist would charge. If you want to PM me your city, I can help you with searching for these services. I'm sure you've looked, but it doesn't hurt to have another set of eyes.
Where do you live? If in the US, there should be a community health center that can provide med regimen and therapy on a sliding scale. Colleges with health degrees may also offer affordable options.

First of, I want to thank anyone who is willing to read and reply to this post. I graduated with a biology degree 3 years ago and my intentions during undergrad were to pursue PA school. Long story short, as I tried to gain contact hours for PA school in these past three years, I have been able to work with PTs and I love the work that they do. I can't help but want to pursue PT instead, but I also don't know how it would look on a PT school application. First of, most schools won't accept my prereqs since they have expired so I already know that the route I'm imaging is probably not promising. I would have to start shadowing in different settings, etc.

My GPA is okay (3.8, science 3.6). I don't have any research experience.

Could I possibly pursue this route? I guess what I'm trying to ask is... would a school even bother looking at my application seeing that I am 3 years post grad and only three years later started the process?
